entities.summary: Jasbir K. Puar is an American academic and author. She is Professor and Graduate Director of Women's and Gender Studies at Rutgers University. Her most recent book is The Right to Maim: Debility, Capacity, Disability (2017). She has written on South Asian diasporic cultural production in the United States, United Kingdom and Trinidad, LGBT tourism, terrorism studies, surveillance studies, biopolitics and necropolitics, disability and debilitation, theories of intersectionality, affect, and assemblage; animal studies and posthumanism, homonationalism, pinkwashing, and the Palestinian territories.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent scholar of queer theory and critical disability studies, Jasbir Puar's work has significantly shaped the fields of intersectionality, affect, and posthumanism, influencing academic discourse on issues such as terrorism, surveillance, and biopolitics. Her research has also contributed to a deeper understanding of the intersections between disability, debilitation, and necropolitics.
